messages.subject: Issue with micro_era5 in a loop: "Error in R_nc4_open: Too many open files"
parts:
Good day Mike!

I’m running micro_era5() with coastal=TRUE, cad.effects=TRUE, shore=1. It works well but when I loop the function (360 combinations of slope and aspects x 2 reflectivity values x 10 years x 9 sites) I get this error message after 42 iterations:

...
Applying coastal effects 
running microclimate model for  365  days from  2017-01-01  to  2017-12-31 23:00:00  at site  long -3.349536 lat 59.066536 
Note: the output column `SOLR` in metout and shadmet is for unshaded solar radiation adjusted for slope, aspect and horizon angle 
   user  system elapsed 
   3.44    0.02    3.46 
downloading DEM via package elevatr 
extracting weather data locally from C:/Users/MYPATH/Spatial_Data_Era5/era5_NEB 
Error in R_nc4_open: Too many open files
Error in nc_open(nc) : 
  Error in nc_open trying to open file C:/Users/MYPATH/Spatial_Data_Era5/era5_NEB_2017.nc

I tried to use the following within the loop but it did not fix the problem.

closeAllConnections()
closeAllNcfiles()

Do you have an idea?

Best,

Jonathan

​

messages.author: 6824c1e1fe15ab15
messages.subject: Re: Issue with micro_era5 in a loop: "Error in R_nc4_open: Too many open files"
parts:
I know this was a while ago, but I've come up with a decent solution for this problem without needing to use a for loop. Restarting the R session allows R to clear all of the open connections to the nc files, so we need a way to allow R to restart the session while keeping the loop going. The package rstudioapi has the function restartSession(), and inside the restartSession function you can tell it to call to your current script and run it again after restarting. If you save the iteration number that you are currently on plus one (so if you're on iteration 1, you save a 2) to another directory before you restart the session, R will check on that number after restarting and keep going right where it left off (as long as you use the variable you saved it as in place of the looping variable).

See example code here, which I took from this link (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48305203/restart-r-session-without-interrupting-the-for-loop): 

#Save an the iteration as a separate .RData file in the working directory. 
 iter <- 1 save(iter, file="iter.RData")

Create a script which calls itself for a certain number of iterations. Save the following script as "test_script.R"

###load iteration
library(rstudioapi)
load("iter.RData")
###insert function here.
time_now <- Sys.time()
###save output of function to a file.
save(time_now, file=paste0("time_", iter, ".Rdata"))
###update iteration
iter <- iter+1
save(iter, file="iter.RData")
###restart session calling the script again
if(iter < 5){ 
restartSession(command='source("test_script.R")') }
